questions.stem: Low cortisol, high corticotropin, and dark skin. Where is the failure?

options.text: In the adrenal gland itself (primary)
In the pituitary, which would raise corticotropin
Only in the distal tubule
Only in the placenta

questions.explanation: Primary adrenal failure raises corticotropin and can darken the skin. A pituitary cause would not.

questions.stem: The best first lab when you suspect acromegaly is:

options.text: A single random growth-hormone level
Insulin-like growth factor one
A prolactin only, and stop there
A thyroid-stimulating hormone, and stop there

questions.explanation: Growth hormone pulses. The growth factor does not.

options.text: Start insulin now, and fix potassium later
Replete potassium before insulin
Stop all fluids
Treat only until the sugar is normal

questions.explanation: If potassium is under 3.5, fix it first. Treat until the ketoacidosis is gone, not just until the sugar falls.

questions.stem: A high prolactin should first prompt you to exclude:

options.text: Pregnancy and drugs
Only a uric acid stone
Only a lens-shaped bleed
Only a 3-hertz absence pattern

questions.explanation: A high prolactin is high until pregnancy and drugs are excluded.

questions.stem: A long-standing high thyroid-stimulating hormone can:

options.text: Enlarge the pituitary, so a sellar mass is not always a primary tumor
Never affect the sella
Always cause a lens-shaped epidural bleed
Always raise uric acid stones

questions.explanation: Thyrotroph hyperplasia can mimic a tumor.

options.text: Progesterone first, then a follicle, with no estrogen
Follicle growth, estrogen, a luteinizing surge, then progesterone
Only a random growth-hormone pulse
Only a high anion gap

questions.stem: In diabetic ketoacidosis, treatment should continue until:

options.text: The sugar falls, even if ketones remain
The ketoacidosis itself is gone, not just the sugar
The first bag of fluid is hung, then stop
The prolactin is normal

questions.explanation: The gap and the ketones tell you when you are done.

questions.stem: If an adrenal enzyme is blocked, the useful questions are:

options.text: What hormone is missing, and what is piling up?
Only whether the stone is radiolucent
Only the FEV1 ratio
Only the middle-meningeal artery

questions.explanation: Follow the pile-up, and the enzyme declares itself.

questions.stem: A pituitary cause of low cortisol would typically have:

options.text: A high corticotropin and bronze skin
A low corticotropin, without that bronze skin
Always a high anion-gap ketoacidosis
Always a lens-shaped bleed

questions.explanation: Both hormones are low, and the skin does not bronze from this.

options.text: Primary adrenal failure: low cortisol, high corticotropin, skin can darken.
Screen acromegaly with a random growth-hormone level only.
If potassium is under 3.5 in ketoacidosis, replete it before insulin.
Exclude pregnancy and drugs before chasing a high prolactin.

questions.explanation: Acromegaly is screened with insulin-like growth factor one, because growth hormone pulses.
